subtitle: Writing a review, and reading a poem
words.intro: German literary criticism has a word for everything, and little patience. A review on the arts pages can make a career, or end one. And somewhere on the same page there’s a poem, short, with an ant in it, which is what everyone will remember.

grammar[0].blocks[1].root.q: Is the book the subject of the sentence?
grammar[0].fact: *Das Buch handelt von Liebe*, the book is about love. *Es handelt sich um einen Roman*, it’s a novel. Don’t mix them: the second has no subject but *es*, and native writers still go wrong. Marcel Reich-Ranicki, the best known of German critics, was a TV star. His judgments could make a novel into a best-seller, or end it.

grammar[1].fact: Every word in those six lines is one you learned before B1. That’s worth a moment. You could have read this poem a long time ago, but you’d have had the words, not the joke. *Weise* carries it: wise. It’s what you call giving up, when you’re a very small ant.

document.intro: A real title page, from Leipzig, of an almanac called, for reasons not given, the *Ant Calendar*. It’s in its 59th year, and comes with four free supplements. A full review would be longer. Try writing one in only one sentence.
document.fact: Family almanacs like this one sold in great numbers in the 19th century, with stories, farming hints and sayings. Ringelnatz’s ants, unlike these, never got as far as Leipzig.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Write a very short review of the calendar.
document.tasks[1].note: Your own review. Be kind to the ants.
reading.intro: Maya’s novel has come out. A short review has appeared in a big paper, by the feared critic Wolf Reinhardt. The Hofstraße has read it together on the stairs. Maya has read it nine times and doesn’t know if it’s good or bad.
reading.fact: Joachim Ringelnatz, the pen name of Hans Bötticher, was a sailor, a painter and a poet who performed his verse in cabarets. The Nazis banned him from performing, and he died in 1934. *Die Ameisen* is six lines long, and many Germans know it by heart.
